text.p: Philips Electronics NV on Wednesday reiterated its targets of double-digit growth in operating income, a positive cashflow of over one billion guilders in 1997 and a 24 percent return on net assets (RONA) in the longer term.
"The first-quarter results provide us with the confidence that we are on track following the improvement programme started in 1996," Philips said in a statement.
"A number of restructuring programmes which are still underway should begin to contribute to profits over the next several quarters," it added.

"We remain committed to achieving our previously announced goals of double-digit growth in operating income, a positive cashflow of over one billion guilders in 1997, and a 24 percent return on net assets (RONA) in the longer term."
